name: CUORE
full_name: Cryogenic Underground Observatory for Rare Events
summary: CUORE is a large cryogenic array searching for tellurium-130 neutrinoless double-beta decay at Gran Sasso. Its unsegmented crystal calorimeters also measure two-neutrino decay and other rare processes.
detection_principle: TeO2 crystals operated near 10 mK convert deposited energy into a small temperature rise. Thermistors measure the heat pulses; anticoincidence between crystals suppresses events depositing energy at several locations.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The CUORE neutrinoless-double-beta data-taking programme ended on 9 June 2026. INFN reported the completed scientific programme and its 5 October celebration after reaching 3 tonne-years of crystal exposure.

timeline.event: Celebrated the completed scientific programme after 3 tonne-years of crystal exposure.

collaboration.name: CUORE Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: Physics operation began in 2017; published searches constrain the 130Te neutrinoless-decay half-life.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
